items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1958-05-31
items.q: I worked with him in Chicago. I worked with him in New Orleans. ... My last recording was with Richard Miney Jones on the Decca Company.

ctx.x: Buddy Johnson trombone player. I worked with him. The time Manion sent me on job with him. He was a very nice fellow inspiration. Quiet guy. Little bit of fellow he was. He played with Manion Barrett's brass man too, don't forget. Played all those marches. He ain't doing marches. Just imagine what Manion had. Big gas for Buddy Johnson trombone and Joe Field. Three devils up in front there. Now you know he had some good men, eh? Yeah. That's why they call it the Imperial Brass Band. But they're all good musicians.…
There's a couple other men here. Richard M. Jones, Miney. Miney Jones.

I worked with him in Chicago. I worked with him in New Orleans. Well, you know yourself. My last recording was with Richard Miney Jones on the Decca Company. That was the last record I made with Jimmy Noon and Johnny Dodson. And both of them died.
